statement: This record remains negative evidence on build 26200.8246: the repo did not produce enough supporting proof to promote it into a normal actionable surface.

anticheat_risk.anticheat_details: Timer-check flags are kernel timer validation surfaces; review is required before applying near anti-cheat or DRM workloads.

gating_reason: Cross-layer evidence is strong, but an explicit policy or supportability gate still blocks promotion.

links.title: Repo system docs assign TimerCheckFlags = 1
links.summary: Repo docs assign `TimerCheckFlags = 1` and map it to `KeTimerCheckFlags` under `Session Manager\\Kernel`.

links.title: Observed baseline existence for TimerCheckFlags
links.summary: The observed clean baseline confirmed that `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel` exists while `TimerCheckFlags` itself is absent.

links.title: Current-build string hit for TimerCheckFlags
links.summary: The broad current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `TimerCheckFlags` in `C:\\Windows\\System32\\ntoskrnl.exe` and no adjacent hits in the supporting `smss.exe`, `winload.exe`, or `ci.dll` probes.

links.title: WRK source-enrichment retains KeTimerCheckFlags initialization and bit-test semantics
links.summary: The later source-enrichment pass retained WRK-backed hits for `extern ULONG KeTimerCheckFlags;`, `ULONG KeTimerCheckFlags = KE_TIMER_CHECK_FREES;`, and `if ((KeTimerCheckFlags & KE_TIMER_CHECK_FREES) == 0) {`, which strongly supports the repo-doc default of `1` as a timer-check bit-enabled state.

links.title: Lightweight runtime batch wrote TimerCheckFlags = 1 and rebooted once
links.summary: The tools-hardened lightweight runtime batch wrote `TimerCheckFlags = 1`, rebooted once, preserved shell health, and still returned `zero-exact-target-hits` for this specific candidate in the compact runtime results.

links.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD bundle resolves KeTimerCheckFlags = 1
links.summary: A dedicated live KVM local-KD bundle resolved `nt!KeTimerCheckFlags` and directly read the running current-build value as `1`.
